source: Dış kaynaklarda saptanan eksik soru tipleri; bağımsız anlatım ve resmî cevap kontrolü (2026-10-13)
answer_convention: İki dilde aynı sırada; ilk şık doğru. Belirsiz cevap aktif bankada yok.
id_convention: Kalıcı idler_080.json; eski veya emekli kimlik yeniden kullanılmaz.

questions.text: An aeroplane is below the AFM/POH manoeuvring speed (VA) for its actual mass, in smooth air. Which statement about the structural protection associated with VA is correct?
options: It does not cover repeated full reversals or simultaneous full inputs on multiple axes.
It permits repeated full reversals whenever only one control axis is used.
It permits simultaneous full inputs on several control axes in smooth air.
It makes the allowable control inputs independent of the current aircraft mass.

questions.text: For the same mass, configuration, centre of gravity, load factor and power condition, a light aeroplane reaches a higher altitude where air density is lower. At low subsonic speeds, neglecting instrument, position and compressibility errors, how do its stall IAS and stall TAS compare?
options: Stall IAS is approximately unchanged; stall TAS is higher.
Stall IAS is higher; stall TAS is approximately unchanged.
Stall IAS is lower; stall TAS is higher.
Both stall IAS and stall TAS are approximately unchanged.

questions.text: A propeller accelerates air rearward. Which principle explains the corresponding forward reaction force on the aeroplane?
options: Newton’s third law: equal and opposite forces.
Newton’s first law: no force is required for acceleration.
Boyle’s law: every volume decrease must produce forward thrust.
The aircraft weight must equal its engine thrust.

questions.text: What is the general aerodynamic effect of raising a spoiler on a wing?
options: It disrupts the airflow, reducing lift and increasing drag.
It increases lift and decreases drag like an ideal leading-edge slot.
It increases camber and wing area like a Fowler flap.
It increases thrust by feeding more air to the propeller.

questions.text: A T-tail may be clear of the wing wake in normal flight. At a sufficiently high angle of attack, what serious condition can occur?
options: The wing wake can blanket the high tailplane and reduce elevator effectiveness.
The tailplane automatically creates unlimited nose-down control.
The rudder becomes the main pitch control because its hinge is vertical.
The tailplane location guarantees that the aircraft cannot stall.

questions.text: On the independently plotted coefficient polar, which labelled point represents the maximumCL and therefore the critical angle of attack for this illustrated aerofoil?
options: R.
P.
Q.
S.

questions.text: A wing keeps the same geometric incidence along its span but uses different aerofoil sections so the tip reaches its stall later than the root. What is this design feature called?
options: Aerodynamic washout.
Geometric washout.
Wing anhedral.
Forward sweep.

questions.text: What is meant by boundary-layer separation from an aerofoil?
options: The near-surface airflow breaks away from the aerofoil instead of following its contour.
The laminar flow becomes turbulent while remaining attached to the contour.
The oncoming flow divides into upper and lower paths at the leading edge.
The total pressure is added to the static pressure inside the pitot tube.

questions.text: What is the transition point in the boundary layer over an aerofoil?
options: The location where laminar boundary-layer flow becomes turbulent.
The location where all aerodynamic forces are represented as acting.
The point where the freestream velocity must be exactly zero.
The point where attached airflow has already separated from the surface.

questions.text: After a roll disturbance, an aeroplane with positive wing dihedral sideslips towards its lower wing. What creates the restoring rolling moment?
options: The sideslip increases the lower wing’s effective AOA and lift relative to the upper wing.
The lower wing loses all lift while the upper wing gains lift.
The rudder becomes a horizontal lifting surface as soon as bank develops.
Gravity applies a direct rolling moment about the CG even without an aerodynamic force change.

questions.text: For the same air density, reference area, configuration and angle of attack, assume Reynolds-number and compressibility effects on CD are negligible. When airflow speed doubles, which statement about parasite drag and its coefficient is correct?
options: Parasite drag becomes four times as large; its coefficient remains approximately unchanged.
Parasite drag and its coefficient both become four times as large.
Parasite drag doubles; its coefficient also doubles.
Parasite drag stays unchanged; its coefficient becomes one quarter as large.

questions.text: In the drag-versus-speed diagram, which labelled curve shows parasite drag?
options: B
A
C
The vertical axis

questions.text: In the drag-versus-speed diagram, which labelled curve shows total drag?
options: C
A
B
The horizontal axis

questions.text: Which motion characterises Dutch roll?
options: A coupled oscillation in roll and yaw.
A pure pitching oscillation with no lateral motion.
An increase in bank angle with no oscillation, followed by a spiral dive.
A vertical bounce of the landing gear while the aircraft is parked.

questions.text: During straight flight, before the pilot reacts, what is the usual immediate load-factor response to (1) an upward vertical gust and (2) a downward vertical gust?
options: (1) Increases; (2) decreases.
(1) Decreases; (2) increases.
(1) Unchanged; (2) unchanged.
(1) Decreases; (2) decreases.

questions.text: Comparing otherwise similar aeroplanes with zero geometric dihedral, what is the usual contribution of placing the wing high on the fuselage rather than low?
options: A greater stabilising dihedral effect in sideslip.
A complete elimination of all yawing moments.
A reversal of elevator operation from pitch to roll.
A requirement that the lower wing stall in every normal turn.

questions.text: How can a control surface be aerodynamically balanced to reduce the force needed to deflect it?
options: Place some surface area ahead of its hinge line so air loads assist deflection.
Add all the balancing mass behind the hinge line to increase flutter tendency.
Fit an antiservo tab which always increases hinge force.
Move the centre of gravity beyond the aircraft’s aft limit.

questions.text: Where is interference drag typically generated on an aeroplane?
options: At junctions such as the wing-fuselage intersection, where different airflows interact.
Only at the tyre-ground contact while the aircraft is parked.
Only inside the sealed fuel tanks.
Only when the engine has stopped and the propeller is windmilling.

questions.text: The control column is moved right in an aeroplane with mechanically linked balance tabs. The left aileron moves down. How does its balance tab move relative to the left aileron?
options: Up, opposing the aileron deflection and reducing control force.
Down, following the aileron and increasing control force.
It stays at a fixed angle to the aileron like a simple set trim tab.
It moves only if the elevator trim wheel is rotated.

questions.text: Compared with straight-and-level flight at the same airspeed, what is normally required to maintain both altitude and airspeed in a steady coordinated level turn?
options: A higher angle of attack and enough additional power to overcome the increased drag.
The same angle of attack with power reduced to match the lower drag.
A lower angle of attack and lower power because total lift is smaller.
A higher angle of attack with no possible change in required power.

questions.text: An aeroplane weighing4,600 lbf makes a steady, coordinated, altitude-maintaining 50° banked turn. Approximately what total aerodynamic lift is required?
In a steady coordinated level turn, an aeroplane’s positive load-factor limit is+2.5. Ignoring gusts and other constraints, what is the greatest bank angle that does not exceed this limit?
options: Approximately 66°.
Approximately 45°.
Approximately 75°.

questions.text: An aeroplane tends to fly right-wing-low with the controls released. It has a conventional adjustable trim tab on the left aileron and mechanically linked ailerons. What trim-tab movement produces a correcting left-roll tendency?
options: Tab down, left aileron up and right aileron down.
Tab up, left aileron down and right aileron up.
Tab down, both ailerons down by equal amounts.
Tab up, both ailerons up by equal amounts.

questions.text: At low subsonic speed, neglecting instrument and position error, density changes while an aeroplane keeps the same IAS, wing configuration and angle of attack. What happens to aerodynamic lift and drag?
options: They remain approximately unchanged because the dynamic pressure is unchanged.
Both increase in direct proportion to density.
Lift increases while drag decreases because IAS is unchanged.
Lift decreases while drag increases because TAS must increase.

questions.text: The mass of an aeroplane increases by 20%, with wing area, configuration, CG position and maximum lift coefficient unchanged. Approximately how much does its 1-g stall speed increase?
options: About 10%.
About 20%.
About 44%.
It remains unchanged.

questions.text: For comparable size, speed and other conditions, why does a streamlined body normally have less form drag than a blunt body?
options: It promotes smoother airflow and reduces the separated wake.
It eliminates all skin friction because air viscosity becomes zero.
It produces extra lift so induced drag necessarily becomes zero.
It raises the total mass so the body no longer experiences aerodynamic force.

questions.text: Compared with a laminar boundary layer under otherwise similar conditions, a turbulent boundary layer generally has which trade-off?
options: More skin-friction drag but greater resistance to separation in an adverse pressure gradient.
Less skin-friction drag and less resistance to separation.
No skin-friction drag and immediate separation at every AOA.
The same friction but no near-surface velocity gradient.

questions.text: After engine failure, what is the general aerodynamic effect of a windmilling propeller compared with the powered propeller’s thrust-producing role?
options: It produces drag that reduces glide performance.
It continues to provide normal positive engine thrust.
It eliminates all aerodynamic drag from the aircraft.
It increases lift without affecting the aircraft’s energy.

questions.text: Consider the wing’s contribution alone: its aerodynamic centre is ahead of the aircraft’s CG. If an increase in angle of attack increases wing lift, what incremental pitching effect does that lift change produce?
options: A nose-up moment that tends to reinforce the angle-of-attack increase.
A nose-down moment that necessarily stabilises the complete aircraft.
No moment because every lift force passes through the CG.
Only a yawing moment, because pitch is controlled solely by the rudder.

questions.text: What does wing loading express?
options: Aircraft weight divided by wing area.
Wing span divided by mean chord.
Lift divided by aircraft weight.
Drag divided by available engine power.
